column3: “Struck down of wine” is rendered “overcome with wine.”
“A mighty and strong one” is rendered “a strong and mighty agent,” and “will thrust down” as “has cast it down.”
“He swallows it” keeps the image; NASB adds “as soon as.”
“Those who turn back battle at the gate” is rendered “those who repel the onslaught at the gate.”
The past tenses are rendered as present (“reel,” “stagger”).
“Vomit, filth” is rendered “filthy vomit,” and “not room” as “without a single clean place.”
“Command to command” (tsav latsav) is rendered “Order on order,” and NASB supplies “He says.”
“Here I he has laid” is rendered “Behold, I am laying,” and “will not make haste” as “will not be disturbed”; NASB adds “in it.”
NASB adds “Grain for” and “eventually damage it,” and repeats “He does not thresh it longer”; the Hebrew is terse.
